_meta.method: complete direct literal rendering; source order preserved; no explanatory paraphrase

word_for_word: ननु वेदोक्तनानाफलपरित्यागेन निष्कामतयेश्वराराधनविषया व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिस्तु कुबुद्धिरेवेत्याशङ्क्याह यावानिति

objection: resolute understanding directed toward worship of the Lord without desire, abandoning the many fruits taught by the Vedas, would itself be bad understanding; anticipating this he says ‘as much as’
उदकं पीयतेऽस्मिन्नित्युदपानं वापीकूपतडागादि
an ‘udapāna’ is a reservoir, well, pond, and the like from which water is drunk
तस्मिन्स्वल्पोदके एकत्र कृत्स्नस्यार्थस्याभावात्तत्र परिभ्रमणेन विभागशो यावान्स्नानपानादिरर्थः प्रयोजनं भवति
because in such small bodies of water all purposes are not found in one place, one must wander among them to obtain separately purposes such as bathing and drinking
तावान्सर्वोऽप्यर्थः सर्वतःसंप्लुतोदके महाह्रदे एकत्रैव यथा भवति
all those purposes exist together in one great lake filled with water on every side
एवं यावान्सर्वेषु वेदेषु तत्तकर्मफलरूपोऽर्थस्तावान्सर्वोऽपि विजानतो व्यवसायात्मिकबुद्धियुक्तस्य ब्राह्मणस्य ब्रह्मनिष्ठस्य भवत्येव
so all the purposes in all the Vedas in the form of the respective fruits of action are present for the discerning brāhmaṇa endowed with resolute understanding and established in Brahman
ब्रह्मानन्दे क्षुद्रानन्दानामन्तर्भूतत्वात्
because lesser pleasures are included within the bliss of Brahman
एतस्यैवानन्दस्यान्यानि भूतानि मात्रामुपजीवन्ति इति श्रुतेः
as Śruti says, ‘other beings live upon only a fraction of this bliss’
तस्मादियमेव बुद्धिः सुबुद्धिरित्यर्थः
therefore this understanding alone is good understanding; this is the meaning
तर्हि सर्वकर्मफलानि परमेश्वराराधनादेव भविष्यन्तीत्यभिसंधाय प्रवर्तेत किं कर्मणेत्याशङ्क्य तद्वारयन्नाह कर्मण्येवेति
objection: then one might act thinking that all fruits of action will come merely from worship of the Supreme Lord; why act at all? preventing this, he says ‘only in action’
ते तव तत्त्वज्ञानार्थिनः कर्मण्येवाधिकारः
for you, who seek knowledge of reality, there is authority only regarding action
तत्फलेषु बन्धहेतुष्वधिकारः कामो मास्तु
let there be no authority, no desire, regarding its fruits, which are causes of bondage
ननु कर्मणि कृते तत्फलं स्यादेव भोजने कृते तृप्तिवदित्याशङ्क्याह मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूः
objection: when action is performed its fruit surely occurs, just as eating produces satisfaction; anticipating this he says ‘do not become the cause of the fruit of action’
कर्मफलं प्रवृत्तिहेतुर्यस्य तथाभूतो मा भूः
do not become one for whom the fruit of action is the motive for activity
कामितस्यैव स्वर्गादेर्नियोज्यविशेषणत्वेन फलत्वादकामितं फलं न स्यादिति भावः
because heaven and the like count as fruits only when desired and thus qualify the person enjoined, an undesired result is not a fruit in that sense; this is the intention
अतएव फलं बन्धकं भविष्यतीति भयादकर्मणि कर्माकरणेऽपि तव सङ्गो निष्ठा मास्तु
therefore, from fear that fruit will bind, do not become attached or committed even to non-action, the failure to perform action
किं तर्हि योगस्थ इति
what then? he says ‘established in yoga’
योगः परमेश्वरैकपरता तत्र स्थितः कर्माणि कुरु
yoga is single-minded orientation toward the Supreme Lord; established in that, perform actions
तथा सङ्गं कर्तृत्वाभिनिवेशं त्यक्त्वा केवलमीश्वराश्रयेणैव कुरु
likewise, abandoning attachment, the insistence on being the doer, act relying on the Lord alone
तत्फलस्य ज्ञानस्यापि सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा केवलमीश्वरार्पणेनैव कुरु
remaining equal regarding success and failure even of knowledge, the fruit of such action, act solely by offering it to the Lord
यत एवंभूतं समत्वमेव योग उच्यते सद्भिः
for equality of this kind is what the wise call yoga
चित्तसमाधानरूपत्वात्
because it has the form of composure of mind
काम्यं तु कर्मातिनिकृष्टमित्याह दूरेणेति
he says that desire-motivated action is exceedingly inferior with ‘by far’
बुद्ध्या व्यवसायात्मिकया कृतः कर्मयोगो बुद्धियोगः
karma-yoga performed with resolute understanding is ‘buddhi-yoga’
बुद्धिसाधनभूतो वा
or it is that which serves as a means to knowledge
तस्मात्सकाशादन्यत्काम्यं कर्म दूरेणावरमत्यन्तमपकृष्टम्
compared with it, other desire-motivated action is far inferior, extremely low
हि यस्मादेवं तस्माद्बुद्धौ ज्ञाने शरणमाश्रयं कर्मयोगमन्विच्छानुतिष्ठ
because this is so, seek and practice karma-yoga as the refuge, the support, for understanding, knowledge
यद्वा बुद्धौ शरणं त्रातारमीश्वरमाश्रयेत्यर्थः
or: take refuge in the protector, the Lord, within understanding; this is the meaning
फलहेतवस्तु सकामा नराः कृपणा दीनाः
persons motivated by fruits, acting with desire, are pitiable, wretched
यो वा एतदक्षरं गार्ग्यविदित्वास्माल्लोकात्प्रैति स कृपणः इति श्रुतेः
as Śruti says: ‘O Gārgī, whoever departs this world without knowing this Imperishable is pitiable’
बुद्धियोगयुक्तस्तु श्रेष्ठ इत्याह बुद्धीति
he says that one endowed with buddhi-yoga is superior with ‘endowed with understanding’
सुकृतं स्वर्गादिप्रापकम् दुष्कृतं निरयादिप्रापकम् ते उभे इहैव जन्मनि परमेश्वरप्रसादेन जहाति त्यजति
good action leading to heaven and the like and bad action leading to hell and the like—both are abandoned, cast off, here in this very birth through the grace of the Supreme Lord
तस्माद्योगाय तदर्थाय कर्मयोगाय युज्यस्व घटस्व
therefore apply yourself, strive, for yoga, for karma-yoga serving that purpose
यतः कर्मसु यत्कौशलं बन्धकानामपि तेषामीश्वराराधनेन मोक्षपरत्वसंपादनचातुर्यं स एव योगः
for skill in actions means the dexterity by which even binding actions are made conducive to liberation through worship of the Lord; that itself is yoga
कर्मणां मोक्षसाधनत्वप्रकारमाह कर्मेति
he states how actions become a means to liberation with ‘action-born’
कर्मजं फलं त्यक्त्वा केवलमीश्वराराधनार्थमेव कर्म कुर्वाणा
performing action only for worship of the Lord, abandoning the fruit born of action
मनीषिणो ज्ञानिनो भूत्वा
becoming discerning, becoming knowers
जन्मरूपेण बन्धेन विनिर्मुक्ताः सन्तः
being completely freed from bondage in the form of birth
अनामयं सर्वोपद्रवरहितं विष्णोः पदं मोक्षाख्यं गच्छन्ति
they reach the state of Viṣṇu called liberation, free from affliction, devoid of all calamity
कदा तत्पदमहं प्राप्स्यामीत्यपेक्षायामाह यदेति द्वाभ्याम्
when it is asked ‘when shall I attain that state?’ he replies in the two verses beginning ‘when’
मोहो देहादिष्वात्मबुद्धि तदेव कलिलं कलिलं गहनं विदुः इत्यभिधानकोशस्मृतेः
delusion is the cognition of the Self in the body and the like; that itself is ‘kalila,’ a thicket, according to the lexicon ‘they know kalila as dense’
एवं परमेश्वराराधने क्रियमाणे यदा तत्प्रसादेन तव बुद्धिर्देहाभिमानलक्षणं मोहमयं गहनं दुर्गं विशेषेणातितरिष्यति
when, as worship of the Supreme Lord is thus performed, your understanding through His grace thoroughly crosses the difficult thicket of delusion characterized by identification with the body
तदा श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्यार्थस्य च निर्वेदं वैराग्यं गन्तासि प्राप्स्यसि
then you will attain dispassion, detachment, toward what is to be heard and toward the meaning of what has been heard
तयोरनुपादेयत्वेन जिज्ञासां न करिष्यसीत्यर्थः
you will no longer inquire after them because they are not to be taken up; this is the meaning
ततश्च श्रुतीति
and then, with ‘by what has been heard’
श्रुतिभिर्नानालौकिकवैदिकार्थश्रवणैर्विप्रतिपन्ना इतः पूर्वं विक्षिप्ता सती तव बुद्धिः
your understanding, previously distracted and pulled in different directions by hearing many worldly and Vedic matters
यदा समाधौ स्थास्यतीति समाधीयते चित्तमस्मिन्निति समाधिः परमेश्वरः
when it stands in samādhi—‘samādhi’ here is the Supreme Lord, in whom the mind is composed
तस्मिन्निश्चला विक्षेपव्याप्तिविषयान्तरैरनाकृष्टा
unmoving in Him, not drawn away by other objects through distraction
अत एवाचला अभ्यासपटुत्वेन तत्रैव स्थिरा लयव्याप्तिः सती
and therefore immovable, remaining firm there through proficiency born of practice, not overcome by dissolution
तदा योगं योगफलं तत्त्वज्ञानमवाप्स्यसि
then you will attain yoga, the fruit of yoga, knowledge of reality
पूर्वश्लोकोक्तस्यात्मतत्त्वज्ञस्य लक्षणं जिज्ञासुः अर्जुन उवाच स्थितप्रज्ञस्येति
desiring to know the characteristics of the knower of the Self described in the previous verse, Arjuna spoke with ‘of one of steady wisdom’
स्वाभाविके समाधौ स्थितस्य अत एव स्थिता निश्चला प्रज्ञा बुद्धिर्यस्य तस्य का भाषा
what is the ‘bhāṣā,’ the description, of one established in natural samādhi and whose wisdom, understanding, is therefore steady and unmoving?
भाष्यतेऽनयेति भाषा लक्षणमिति यावत्
‘bhāṣā’ is that by which something is described, that is, its characteristic
केन लक्षणेन स्थितप्रज्ञ उच्यत इत्यर्थः
by what characteristic is one called a person of steady wisdom? this is the meaning
तथा स्थितधीः किं कथं भाषणमासनं व्रजनं च कुर्यादित्यर्थः
and how does one of steady understanding speak, sit, and move? this is the meaning
अत्र च यानि साधकस्य ज्ञानसाधनानि तान्येव स्वाभाविकानि सिद्धस्य लक्षणानि
here, the very means to knowledge for the practitioner are the natural characteristics of the accomplished one
अतः सिद्धस्य लक्षणानि कथयन्नेवान्तरङ्गाणि ज्ञानसाधनान्याह यावदध्यायसमाप्ति
therefore, while stating the characteristics of the accomplished one, he simultaneously states the internal means to knowledge through the end of the chapter
तत्र प्रथमप्रश्नोत्तरमाह प्रजहातीति द्वाभ्याम्
there he answers the first question in the two verses beginning ‘abandons’
श्रीभगवानुवाच मनसि स्थितान्कामान्यदा प्रकर्षेण जहाति
the Blessed Lord said: when one completely abandons desires situated in the mind
त्यागे हेतुः आत्मन्येव स्वस्मिन्नेव परमानन्दरूपे आत्मना स्वयमेव तुष्ट इति
the reason for abandoning them is that one is satisfied by oneself in the Self alone, in one’s own nature of supreme bliss
आत्मारामः सन्यदा क्षुद्रविषयाभिलाषांस्त्यजति तदा तेन लक्षणेन मुनिः स्थितप्रज्ञ उच्यत इत्यर्थः
when, delighting in the Self, the sage abandons desires for petty objects, by that characteristic he is called one of steady wisdom; this is the meaning
